feedback: Written before this candidate races. Iteration 1 (±0.03 m, 0.012 m footprint) is the best observed result at 337.5, with 13/20 oval finishes, 1/20 s-bend, 0/20 slalom, and max_error 0.062 to 0.063 m with 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run on the sharp tracks. Iteration 2 (±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing, same controller) dropped to 150.8: oval finishes fell to 0/20, max_error rose to 0.064, so widening span without changing footprint hurt. The Integrator found no speed limit (oval finished in 1.83 s), so the failures are on-line losses on bends. I kept the controller unchanged from iteration 1 and changed nothing except the footprint, so the next race isolates footprint overlap. Decision rules: if line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall to about 0.5 or less and max_error drops below 0.05 m, keep sensor_size 0.016 and try a modest weight-shape change only if oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more with max_error near 0.06 m, the footprint is not the gap; keep the span at ±0.03 m and reduce weights rather than widening. If the oval stops finishing, return to sensor_size 0.012.
requested_changes: Keep the ±0.03 m span at 0.015 m spacing and set sensor_size to 0.016 m. Evidence: iteration 2 showed that span alone worsened every track, while iteration 1 line-loss events of 1.1 to 1.3 per run point to dead zones, so overlapping footprints are the direct test.

If s-bend or slalom still exit with max_error above 0.05 m and line-loss events of 1 or more after the footprint change, try sensor spacing 0.02 m with sensor_size 0.016 m (±0.03 m span, five sensors, weights kept). Evidence: iteration 2 at 0.02 m spacing gave no benefit with a 0.012 m footprint, so this only tests overlap at the wider spacing.
Do not raise wheel_radius yet: the oval completed in 1.83 s in iteration 1, so speed is not the limit. Raise to 0.035 m only if a future run completes with completion_time above about 3 s.
